facts.statement: The genus Caviramus was named in 2006 by Nadia Fröbisch and Jörg Fröbisch.
facts.quote: The genus was in 2006 named by Nadia Fröbisch and Jörg Fröbisch.

facts.statement: Caviramus lived during the Late Triassic in the Northern Calcareous Alps of Switzerland.
facts.quote: Caviramus is a genus of caviramid pterosaur from the Late Triassic (early Rhaetian-age) lower Kössen Formation of the Northern Calcareous Alps of Switzerland.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Caviramus consists of three fragments of the lower jaw containing multicuspate teeth.
facts.quote: The genus is based on holotype PIMUZ A/III 1225, three non-contiguous fragments of a ramus (lower jaw) of the mandible with multicuspate teeth.

facts.statement: Caviramus had between twelve and seventeen teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: The number of teeth is estimated at a minimum of twelve and a maximum of seventeen.

facts.statement: Holes in the front of the lower jaw suggest Caviramus had a soft-tissue structure or keratin covering.
facts.quote: A row of large oval foramina runs parallel to the tooth row; foramina in the form of small holes in the anterior part of the lower jaw suggest some sort of soft-tissue structure, or a keratin covering.

facts.statement: Caviramus had a wingspan of approximately 135 centimeters.
facts.quote: Caviramus had a wingspan of about 135 centimeters (53 in).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Caviramus may have been a terrestrial forager based on its long limbs.
facts.quote: Based on its long limbs, it might have been a terrestrial forager.

facts.statement: Caviramus likely used a soaring mode of flight due to its gracile wings.
facts.quote: Its gracile wings suggested a soaring mode of flight.

facts.statement: Caviramus may have been a piscivore and potentially an underwater hunter.
facts.quote: Caviramus tenía una envergadura de cerca de 135 centímetros, y pudo haber sido un piscívoro, potencialmente un cazador de inmersión.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron classified Caviramus within the family Caviramidae.
facts.quote: In 2020 however, a study upheld by Matthew G. Baron about early pterosaur interrelationships found Caviramus to group with Carniadactylus, Raeticodactylus, and the Austriadraconidae, which in turn were within a clade he called Caviramidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Raeticodactylus filisurensis is a synonym of Caviramus, with differences potentially explained by sex or age.
facts.quote: A 2009 study by Fabio Dalla Vecchia concluded that Raeticodactylus, which is known from a more complete skeleton including lower jaw, probably belong to the same genus, and possibly the same species, if the differences (such as size and the presence of a crest in the Raeticodactylus specimen) are not due to sex or age.

facts.statement: Caviramus lived between 211.18 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (211.18 to 201.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A second specimen reveals Caviramus possessed a tall bony crest on the front of the upper jaw and a keel on the lower jaw.
rejected.quote: The skull shows that it had a tall thin bony crest running along the midline of the front of the upper jaw, and a keel on the lower jaw.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'front of the upper jaw and a keel'
